review.brief:
Review RM29 tier 2: the manualcharge -> charging module rename. Judge the DIFF (fe69cc8 + 4d45c5b + adc4eb7 vs a2f1ffe~1), not the whole module.
1. Behaviour-preservation: this is a pure rename. Any semantic change to logic, SQL, migrations, or test assertions is a blocker. git recorded 12 renames as R - confirm no content drifted inside them beyond package clauses, import paths, qualifiers and error-message prefixes.
2. Completeness of the sweep: no live reference to manualcharge/manualchargedb/ManualCharge* may survive outside deliberately-frozen artifacts. Frozen by design and NOT findings: applied migration 20260815000002_add_charge_gaps.sql (D6/D4), openspec/specs/manual-charge-log/ (D1), archived change folders, historical roadmap/backlog entries. Run a broad case-insensitive sweep yourself (manualcharge, manualChargeWriter/Reader lowercase, pkg.[A-Z] qualifiers) - the leader's first inventory was incomplete and a worker caught 5 misses.
3. Design compliance: check the change against design.md D1-D10 individually, especially D3 (public surface: what renames vs what stays - ManualChargeEntry deliberately untouched), D5 (doc updates verified not assumed), D9 (sqlc hand-move then regenerate; generated files must be byte-identical to a fresh make sqlc).
4. Boundaries (ai/architecture.md): charging owns its own db subpackage; gateway/analytics reach it only through public Go interfaces; no HTML outside gateway; no cross-module DB reads introduced by the rename.
5. Config/build wiring: sqlc.yaml, Makefile MIGRATIONS_DIRS, .air.toml exclude_dir all re-pointed - a miss here fails silently (build stays green, migrations stop applying).
6. Spec deltas: specs/gateway/spec.md and specs/analytics/spec.md. MODIFIED requirements replace the whole body at sync, so verify every acceptance criterion of the main spec survives - one dropped criterion was already caught and restored (D5 in decisions[]). Confirm no other criterion was weakened or lost. Append-only rule is absolute.
7. Docs-track-change (CLAUDE.md non-negotiable): README structure tree + architecture table, module AGENTS.md files, docs/ references all updated in-change.
8. Anti-gaming: no task title, criterion or finding edited/weakened; no self-approved status.
Test-Execution-Policy (verbatim): Claude writes tests but never runs the suite - never go test ./..., make test, make test-with-db or make check. It MAY run go build ./..., go vet ./..., gofmt -l, make build, make vet, make bins, and the standalone guards make ui-guard / make i18n-guard / make money-guard. The owner runs the suite and reports results; work that is complete but unexecuted is awaiting-user-verification, never done, and a passing suite is recorded as the owner's report, never claimed by the assistant.
Signal provenance: ASSISTANT-RUN - go build ./..., go vet ./..., make vet, make bins, make sqlc (idempotency), ui/i18n/money guards, openspec validate --changes --strict (1 passed / 0 failed). OWNER-REPORTED - go test ./... green (5.4) and make migrate-status clean (5.5). Judge test quality by READING the tests; do not run the suite.
Performance-Profile (verbatim): read-heavy - read performance is mandatory over write performance; writes are mostly done by pollers at midnight, so denormalizing, indexing aggressively, and precomputing for reads is acceptable - never at the cost of the modular-monolith boundaries or module data ownership. (D10: satisfied trivially - a rename changes no query shape; confirm that holds.)
Escalate on doubt: return changes-requested rather than approving anything you are unsure of.
